dataset: IQVIA NMTA patient-visit extract (OA and RA visits, place of service)
evidence: PROPOSAL.md 19.1 and the monthly workflow comment: NMTA extracts arrive about 40 days after month end, so month t is known around the 10th of month t+2 (taken as month t+2 in whole months). Not confirmed by IQVIA.
revision_note: One extract only, so there is no earlier vintage to compare and revisions are unknown.
leakage_note: A forecast of month t uses data through t-1, which arrives after month t has ended, so the next-month forecast is for a month already over when the data is known.

dataset: Medicare Part B payment limit (ASP) files
evidence: A file is named for the quarter it applies to and is posted before the quarter starts: the October 2026 file is stamped 091626 (16 September 2026). Taken as the first month of the quarter (the period end month minus two).
revision_note: Files we hold for 2019 and 2020 are later revisions (update stamps 052920, 112420, 022421, 052521 and 090121), so values may differ from first release.
leakage_note: A revised payment limit is not the value known at the time.

dataset: Open Payments general payments (program years 2019 to 2025)
evidence: Each program year is published in June of the following year (assumed from the annual publication cycle). All 7 files we hold carry the stamp P06302026, the June 2026 refresh; the program year 2025 file is documented as published in June 2026.
revision_note: Every year is the June 2026 refresh and includes corrections made after its first publication.
leakage_note: Values for earlier years are corrected values, not what was public in the first June after the year.

dataset: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Geography and Service
evidence: File names carry the release number, and release = data year + 2 for every file (R21 for 2019 data through R26 for 2024 data). Dated documents in the folders show 21 October 2021 and 8 April 2025 (Part B, 2019 and 2023 data) and 21 April 2026 (Part D, 2024 data). December of the release year is taken as the conservative month.
revision_note: A later release can restate an earlier year (version tags V10 and V20 appear in the file names).
leakage_note: Known about two years after the data year, so it can only be a lagged feature.

dataset: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service
evidence: 2019 to 2023 are filtered API pulls of the same annual releases and 2024 is the full release file (PHY_R26). Dated documents in the folders show 21 October 2021 and 8 April 2025 (Part B, 2019 and 2023 data) and 21 April 2026 (Part D, 2024 data). December of the release year is taken as the conservative month.
leakage_note: Prescriber-level and local only; known about two years after the data year.

dataset: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug (optional)

dataset: CDC PLACES county data (2025 release, arthritis prevalence)
evidence: The file is the 2025 release and the loaded data year is 2023; the release month is not in the file and December is taken as the conservative month.
revision_note: A single release: one value per county for every period.
leakage_note: A static covariate, not a time series.

evidence: The file name NPPES_Data_Dissemination_September_2026_V2 is a snapshot of the registry as of September 2026.
leakage_note: Describes the registry today; using it for earlier months leaks the future. Usable only as a current-day denominator.

evidence: Every SEC file name starts with its filing date (YYYY-MM-DD_form_accession_document) and each revenue row carries its source accession.
revision_note: A later filing can restate a figure; the figures are those in the cited filing.
leakage_note: A fourth-quarter figure is derived (the year minus nine months) and known at the 10-K filing date.

dataset: Event timeline (FDA, CMS and other dated documents)
evidence: Each event row has a date and a primary source document.
leakage_note: An event is known on its own date; a scheduled future event was known earlier, which this rule does not capture.
